trigger_desc: Fine density user — heavy butters in top 3
reason: Heavy butters weigh fine hair down, flattening curls and creating a greasy feel.
user_message: We filtered out products with heavy butters because they can weigh down fine hair.

trigger_desc: Fine density user — heavy butters anywhere
reason: Even in lower concentrations, heavy butters can build up over time on fine hair.

trigger_desc: Low porosity user — non-water-soluble silicones in top 5
reason: Non-water-soluble silicones sit on the tight low-porosity cuticle, blocking moisture.
user_message: Low porosity hair absorbs better without heavy silicones — we focused on formulas that let moisture in.

trigger_desc: Low porosity user — mineral oil or petrolatum
reason: Mineral oil and petrolatum create buildup on low porosity hair with no moisture penetration.
user_message: Low porosity hair can get buildup from mineral oil and petrolatum.

trigger_desc: Low porosity user — lightweight oils and humectants in top 5
reason: Lightweight oils penetrate the tight cuticle. Humectants pull moisture in.

trigger_desc: High porosity user — proteins and bond builders
reason: High porosity means the cuticle is raised or damaged — proteins patch it and bond builders repair it.

trigger_desc: High porosity user — leave-in or styler without sealing
reason: High porosity hair loses moisture fast without a sealing layer.

trigger_desc: Relaxed/permed user — clarifying sulfates
reason: Relaxed hair is already porous and protein-compromised. Sulfates strip what remains.
user_message: Since your hair has been relaxed or permed, we prioritized sulfate-free cleansers.

trigger_desc: Color/bleach user — sulfates in top 3
reason: Sulfates strip color molecules and further damage bleached cuticle.
user_message: Color-treated hair keeps its vibrancy longer with sulfate-free shampoos.

trigger_desc: Color/bleach user — bond repair products
reason: Bleach breaks disulfide bonds. Bond repair is the single most important category for this user.
user_message: Bond repair rebuilds the structure bleach breaks down.

trigger_desc: Relaxed/permed user — bond repair
reason: Relaxers break both disulfide and keratin bonds.
user_message: Bond repair helps maintain the integrity of relaxed hair.

trigger_desc: Relaxed/permed user — protein in top 3 on non-treatment
reason: Relaxed hair is sensitive to protein overload in daily products.
user_message: We prioritized moisture-forward products — relaxed hair can get stiff with too much protein.

trigger_desc: Heat styled user — surface bond repair need
reason: Frequent heat damages bonds even when ends look fine.
user_message: Consider adding a bond treatment weekly — heat styling breaks bonds even when ends look healthy.

trigger_desc: Protective styles user — scalp actives
reason: Protective styles often hide scalp buildup and irritation.
user_message: Scalp care is especially important when wearing protective styles.

trigger_desc: Sensitive scalp — fragrance in cleansing/scalp products
reason: Synthetic fragrance is the #1 trigger for scalp irritation and contact dermatitis.
user_message: We only surfaced fragrance-free options for your sensitive scalp.

trigger_desc: Sensitive scalp — formaldehyde releasers
reason: Formaldehyde-releasing preservatives cause scalp irritation and allergic reactions.
user_message: We avoided products with formaldehyde-releasing preservatives.

trigger_desc: Sensitive scalp — strong essential oils in scalp care top 5
reason: High concentrations of essential oils cause burning on sensitive scalps.
user_message: Sensitive scalps can react to strong essential oils — we picked gentler alternatives.

trigger_desc: Oily scalp — clarifying and balancing ingredients in shampoo
reason: These ingredients control sebum production and dissolve scalp buildup.

trigger_desc: Oily scalp — heavy oils in shampoo
reason: Heavy butters in shampoo leave residue on already-oily scalps.

trigger_desc: Dry scalp — nourishing scalp oils
reason: Lightweight and medium oils deliver moisture to a dry scalp without clogging follicles.

trigger_desc: Definition goal + humid climate — glycerin top 5
reason: Glycerin pulls moisture from humid air into hair, causing frizz and loss of definition.
user_message: In high humidity, glycerin can work against curl definition.

trigger_desc: Moisture goal + high porosity — protein + emollient combo
reason: High porosity needs both protein to patch the cuticle and emollients to seal in moisture.

trigger_desc: Length retention + coily — sealing emollients in leave-in/styler/treatment
reason: Coily hair retains length when moisture is sealed in.

trigger_desc: Frizz goal + medium-high porosity — water-soluble silicones in styler
reason: Water-soluble silicones seal the cuticle against humidity without buildup.

trigger_desc: Wavy user — heavy stylers in top 3
reason: Wavy hair loses wave pattern and gets weighed down by heavy stylers.
user_message: We stuck to lighter stylers that support wave pattern.

trigger_desc: Protein overload — 3+ products with PRO-HYD in routine
reason: Stacking too many protein products causes stiffness, brittleness, and breakage.
user_message: Your routine has several protein-rich products — use the treatment no more than once a week.

trigger_desc: Coconut-sensitive user — coconut oil present
reason: Some users experience coconut oil as protein.
user_message: We avoided coconut oil based on your preference.

trigger_desc: 4c + low porosity — heavy butters without humectants
reason: 4c low-porosity hair needs moisture in before sealing. Butters alone sit on top.

trigger_desc: Recent bleach (6mo) — bond repair boost
reason: Fresh bleach damage benefits most from intensive bond repair.
user_message: Since your color is recent, we prioritized bond repair heavily.

trigger_desc: User skipped porosity — assume medium
reason: Without porosity data, default to medium and flag confidence.
user_message: We are using medium porosity as a starting point — as you try products, we will learn what works.
